headline: A proposed class action accuses OpenAI of taking sensitive data from children who used ChatGPT without parental consent and using it to train its AI.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a filed nationwide class action on children's data at the biggest AI chatbot maker, confirmed by several outlets, but the claims are untested and disputed.
importance_line: Children who used ChatGPT and their parents are affected most, and the case could test how AI companies must check ages and treat minors' data, but these are unproven allegations, OpenAI disputes them, and no court has yet decided whether the case can proceed as a class action.
summary: Bloomberg Law reports that a proposed nationwide class action filed on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 in federal court in San Francisco alleges OpenAI designed ChatGPT to manipulate children into sharing personal and health information without the parental consent its own terms require, then used it to train its models and build profiles of them. The suit also asks that affected children receive a proportionate share of OpenAI's equity or its cash equivalent, and OpenAI says it strongly disagrees, pointing to its age-specific protections.
notes: Reuters page (pool source) gave HTTP 401; the same lawsuit was read in Bloomberg Law's own report, with the plaintiffs' ages from the lead of the Daily Journal article. Reuters, Courthouse News, Daily Journal and Law360 also cover it.
